newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed but little changed.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed but little changed.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed but little changed in trading that saw blue chip Banco Ganadero among the day's biggest losers.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.13 percent at 16,712.14 on a trading volume of 1.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB closed down a razor thin 0.01 percent, meanwhile, ending at 1,078.99 on above average volume of 3.9 billion pesos.
Gainers were led by Banco de Bogota, which rose 0.77 percent in the capital to close at 6,350 pesos per share.
Traders said buying, by foreign funds and local investors alike, was fueled by the fact that the bank will pay a healthy dividend at a shareholders' meeting set for next week.
Banco de Colombia, which closed up 0.94 percent in Medellin at 428 pesos per share, was another mover and heavily traded.

The increase came despite the fact that Banco de Colombia's annual shareholders' meeting, set for Friday morning, had to be cancelled after the family-owned bank's top shareholders failed to show up for the meeting.

A senior bank official later told Reuters that the no-show by the Gilinski family, which bought Banco de Colombia in 1994, was due to the fact that they were in Europe negotiating the sale of a stake in the bank to Spain's Banco Central Hispano.

Cementos Argos, which closed up 0.64 percent in Bogota and Compania Suramericana de Seguros, which gained 0.40 percent, were also among winners. Both are owned and managed by the respected Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
Banco Ganadero, which slipped 1.74 percent, and cigarette maker Coltabaco, which ended down 1.43 percent, were the day's biggest victims of profit-taking.
"Their shares had risen very quickly, contrary to stock like Banco de Colombia which has been very slow," one trader said. "People simply decided to take profits."
